*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix)

## `services.pipewire.wireplumber.extraConfig` {#opt-services.pipewire.wireplumber.extraConfig}

Additional configuration for the WirePlumber daemon when run in
single-instance mode (the default in nixpkgs and currently the only
supported way to run WirePlumber configured via `extraConfig`).

See also:

- [The configuration file](https://pipewire.pages.freedesktop.org/wireplumber/daemon/configuration/conf_file.html)
- [Modifying configuration](https://pipewire.pages.freedesktop.org/wireplumber/daemon/configuration/modifying_configuration.html)
- [Locations of files](https://pipewire.pages.freedesktop.org/wireplumber/daemon/configuration/locations.html)
- and the [configuration section](https://pipewire.pages.freedesktop.org/wireplumber/daemon/configuration.html) of the docs in general

Note that WirePlumber (and PipeWire) use dotted attribute names like
`device.product.id`. These are not nested, but flat objects for WirePlumber/PipeWire,
so to write these in nix expressions, remember to quote them like `"device.product.id"`.
Have a look at the example for this.

*Type:* attribute set of attribute set of (JSON value)

*Default:* `{ }`

*Example:*

``` nix
{
  "log-level-debug" = {
    "context.properties" = {
      # Output Debug log messages as opposed to only the default level (Notice)
      "log.level" = "D";
    };
  };
  "wh-1000xm3-ldac-hq" = {
    "monitor.bluez.rules" = [
      {
        matches = [
          {
            # Match any bluetooth device with ids equal to that of a WH-1000XM3
            "device.name" = "~bluez_card.*";
            "device.product.id" = "0x0cd3";
            "device.vendor.id" = "usb:054c";
          }
        ];
        actions = {
          update-props = {
            # Set quality to high quality instead of the default of auto
            "bluez5.a2dp.ldac.quality" = "hq";
          };
        };
      }
    ];
  };
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix)

## `services.pipewire.wireplumber.extraLadspaPackages` {#opt-services.pipewire.wireplumber.extraLadspaPackages}

List of packages that provide LADSPA plugins in `lib/ladspa` that should
be made available to WirePlumber for [filter chains](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/wikis/Filter-Chain).

Config packages have their required LADSPA plugins added automatically,
so they don't need to be specified here. Config packages need to set
`passthru.requiredLadspaPackages` for this to work.

*Type:* list of package

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:* `[ pkgs.noisetorch-ladspa ]`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix)

## `services.pipewire.wireplumber.extraLv2Packages` {#opt-services.pipewire.wireplumber.extraLv2Packages}

List of packages that provide LV2 plugins in `lib/lv2` that should
be made available to WirePlumber for [filter chains](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/wikis/Filter-Chain).

Config packages have their required LV2 plugins added automatically,
so they don't need to be specified here. Config packages need to set
`passthru.requiredLv2Packages` for this to work.

*Type:* list of package

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:* `[ pkgs.lsp-plugins ]`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix)

## `services.pipewire.wireplumber.extraScripts` {#opt-services.pipewire.wireplumber.extraScripts}

Additional scripts for WirePlumber to be used by configuration files.

Every item in this attrset becomes a separate lua file with the path
relative to the `scripts` directory specified in the name of the item.
The scripts get passed to the WirePlumber service via the `XDG_DATA_DIRS`
variable. Scripts specified here are preferred over those shipped with
WirePlumber if they occupy the same relative path.

For a script to be loaded, it needs to be specified as part of a component,
and that component needs to be required by an active profile (e.g. `main`).
Components can be defined in config files either via `extraConfig` or `configPackages`.

For the hello-world example, you'd have to add the following `extraConfig`:

``` nix
  services.pipewire.wireplumber.extraConfig."99-hello-world" = {
    "wireplumber.components" = [
      {
        name = "test/hello-world.lua";
        type = "script/lua";
        provides = "custom.hello-world";
      }
    ];

    "wireplumber.profiles" = {
      main = {
        "custom.hello-world" = "required";
      };
    };
  };
```

See also:

- [Location of scripts](https://pipewire.pages.freedesktop.org/wireplumber/daemon/locations.html#location-of-scripts)
- [Components & Profiles](https://pipewire.pages.freedesktop.org/wireplumber/daemon/configuration/components_and_profiles.html)
- [Migration - Loading custom scripts](https://pipewire.pages.freedesktop.org/wireplumber/daemon/configuration/migration.html#loading-custom-scripts)

*Type:* attribute set of strings concatenated with "\\n"

*Default:* `{ }`

*Example:*

``` nix
{
  "test/hello-world.lua" = ''
    print("Hello, world!")
  '';
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix)

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/desktops/pipewire/wireplumber.nix)

## `services.pixelfed.nginx` {#opt-services.pixelfed.nginx}

With this option, you can customize an nginx virtual host which already has sensible defaults for Pixelfed.
Set to {} if you do not need any customization to the virtual host.
If enabled, then by default, the `serverName` is
`${domain}`,
If this is set to null (the default), no nginx virtualHost will be configured.

*Type:* null or (submodule)

*Default:* `null`

*Example:*

``` nix
{
  serverAliases = [
    "pics.${config.networking.domain}"
  ];
  enableACME = true;
  forceSSL = true;
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix)

## `services.pixelfed.nginx.acmeFallbackHost` {#opt-services.pixelfed.nginx.acmeFallbackHost}

Host which to proxy requests to if ACME challenge is not found. Useful
if you want multiple hosts to be able to verify the same domain name.

With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain
with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would
specify here.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix)

## `services.pixelfed.nginx.acmeRoot` {#opt-services.pixelfed.nginx.acmeRoot}

Directory for the ACME challenge, which is **public**. Don't put certs or keys in here.
Set to null to inherit from config.security.acme.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `"/var/lib/acme/acme-challenge"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix)

Makes this vhost the default.

These lines go to the end of the vhost verbatim.

*Type:* strings concatenated with "\\n"

*Default:* `""`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix)

## `services.pixelfed.nginx.forceSSL` {#opt-services.pixelfed.nginx.forceSSL}

Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults
to 301, configurable with `redirectCode`) all plain HTTP traffic to
HTTPS. This will set defaults for `listen` to listen on all interfaces
on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens
are used for the redirect vhosts.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix)

## `services.pixelfed.nginx.globalRedirect` {#opt-services.pixelfed.nginx.globalRedirect}

If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301,
configurable with `redirectCode`) to the given hostname.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix)

## `services.pixelfed.nginx.http2` {#opt-services.pixelfed.nginx.http2}

Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol.
Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable
HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given
IP address / port.
If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is
enabled for all server blocks on this IP.
See [https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061](https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061).

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix)

## `services.pixelfed.nginx.http3` {#opt-services.pixelfed.nginx.http3}

Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at [https://quic.nginx.org/](https://quic.nginx.org/)
HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix)

## `services.pixelfed.nginx.http3_hq` {#opt-services.pixelfed.nginx.http3_hq}

Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that special application protocol support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at [https://quic.nginx.org/](https://quic.nginx.org/)

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix)

## `services.pixelfed.nginx.kTLS` {#opt-services.pixelfed.nginx.kTLS}

Whether to enable kTLS support.
Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly
reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel.
Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/pixelfed.nix)

## `services.pixelfed.nginx.listen` {#opt-services.pixelfed.nginx.listen}

Listen addresses and ports for this virtual host.
IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in square brackets.
Note: this option overrides `addSSL`
and `onlySSL`.

If you only want to set the addresses manually and not
the ports, take a look at `listenAddresses`.

*Type:* list of (submodule)

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  {
    addr = "195.154.1.1";
    port = 443;
    ssl = true;
  }
  {
    addr = "192.154.1.1";
    port = 80;
  }
  {
```

## `services.plausible.adminUser.email` {#opt-services.plausible.adminUser.email}

Email address of an admin user to seed into the database before the
Plausible web server starts accepting connections.

Plausible Community Edition shows an unauthenticated "first launch"
setup wizard whenever no user exists in the database, which redirects
every page to `/register` and lets anyone reaching the instance over
the network create the first admin account. Setting this option (and
[`services.plausible.adminUser.passwordHashFile`](#opt-services.plausible.adminUser.passwordHashFile)) seeds an
admin user before the port is opened, so the wizard is never reachable
by strangers.

When `null`, no user is seeded and Plausible's setup wizard is used as
usual.

Seeding is idempotent: if any user already exists, no user is created.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Example:* `"admin@example.org"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/plausible.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/plausible.nix)

## `services.plausible.adminUser.name` {#opt-services.plausible.adminUser.name}

Display name of the seeded admin user (see
[`services.plausible.adminUser.email`](#opt-services.plausible.adminUser.email)).

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"Admin"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/plausible.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/plausible.nix)

## `services.plausible.adminUser.passwordHashFile` {#opt-services.plausible.adminUser.passwordHashFile}

Path to a file containing the bcrypt hash of the seeded admin user's
password (see [`services.plausible.adminUser.email`](#opt-services.plausible.adminUser.email)).

Using a hash file (rather than the plaintext password) means the
plaintext never has to be stored on disk or in the Nix store. Generate
a hash e.g. with `mkpasswd -m bcrypt` (the resulting `$2b$...` string).

This file is read via systemd's `LoadCredential`, so it does not enter
the Nix store.

*Type:* null or string or absolute path

*Default:* `null`

*Example:* `"/run/secrets/plausible-admin-password-hash"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/plausible.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/plausible.nix)

## `services.pleroma.configs` {#opt-services.pleroma.configs}

Pleroma public configuration.

This list gets appended from left to
right into /etc/pleroma/config.exs. Elixir evaluates its
configuration imperatively, meaning you can override a
setting by appending a new str to this NixOS option list.

*DO NOT STORE ANY PLEROMA SECRET
HERE*, use
[services.pleroma.secretConfigFile](#opt-services.pleroma.secretConfigFile)
instead.

This setting is going to be stored in a file part of
the Nix store. The Nix store being world-readable, it's not
the right place to store any secret

Have a look to Pleroma section in the NixOS manual for more
information.

*Type:* list of string

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/pleroma.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/pleroma.nix)

## `services.plex.extraPlugins` {#opt-services.plex.extraPlugins}

A list of paths to extra plugin bundles to install in Plex's plugin
directory. Every time the systemd unit for Plex starts up, all of the
symlinks in Plex's plugin directory will be cleared and this module
will symlink all of the paths specified here to that directory.

*Type:* list of absolute path

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  (builtins.path {
    name = "Audnexus.bundle";
    path = pkgs.fetchFromGitHub {
      owner = "djdembeck";
      repo = "Audnexus.bundle";
      rev = "v0.2.8";
      sha256 = "sha256-IWOSz3vYL7zhdHan468xNc6C/eQ2C2BukQlaJNLXh7E=";
    };
  })
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/misc/plex.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/misc/plex.nix)

## `services.plex.extraScanners` {#opt-services.plex.extraScanners}

Every time the systemd unit for Plex starts up, all of the symlinks
in Plex's scanners directory will be cleared and this module will
symlink all of the paths specified here to that directory.

*Type:* list of absolute path

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  (fetchFromGitHub {
    owner = "ZeroQI";
    repo = "Absolute-Series-Scanner";
    rev = "773a39f502a1204b0b0255903cee4ed02c46fde0";
    sha256 = "4l+vpiDdC8L/EeJowUgYyB3JPNTZ1sauN8liFAcK+PY=";
  })
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/misc/plex.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/misc/plex.nix)

## `services.pocket-id.credentials` {#opt-services.pocket-id.credentials}

Credentials which are loaded from the contents of the specified file paths.

This can be used to securely store tokens and secrets outside of the world-readable Nix store.

See [PocketID environment variables](https://pocket-id.org/docs/configuration/environment-variables) (all with the `_FILE` suffix).

Accepts an attrset mapping from the variable name *without its `_FILE` suffix* to the path on disk.

Alternatively you can use `services.pocket-id.environmentFile` to define all the variables in a single file.

*Type:* attribute set of absolute path

*Default:* `{ }`

*Example:*

``` nix
{
  ENCRYPTION_KEY = "/run/secrets/pocket-id/encryption-key";
}
```

## `services.porn-vault.settings` {#opt-services.porn-vault.settings}

Configuration for Porn-Vault. The attributes are serialized to JSON in config.json.

See [https://gitlab.com/porn-vault/porn-vault/-/blob/dev/config.example.json](https://gitlab.com/porn-vault/porn-vault/-/blob/dev/config.example.json)

*Type:* JSON value

*Default:*

``` nix
{
  binaries = {
    ffmpeg = "ffmpeg";
    ffprobe = "ffprobe";
    imagemagick = {
      convert = "convert";
      identify = "identify";
      montage = "montage";
    };
  };
  diagnostics = {
    deadAudioChannelDetection = {
      volumeThreshold = -50;
    };
  };
  import = {
    images = [
      {
        enable = true;
        exclude = [ ];
        extensions = [
          ".jpg"
          ".jpeg"
          ".png"
          ".gif"
        ];
        include = [ ];
        path = "/media/porn-vault/images";
      }
    ];
    videos = [
      {
        enable = true;
        exclude = [ ];
        extensions = [
          ".mp4"
          ".mov"
          ".webm"
        ];
        include = [ ];
        path = "/media/porn-vault/videos";
      }
    ];
  };
  matching = {
    applyActorLabels = true;
    applyStudioLabels = true;
    ignoreSingleNames = true;
    regexAliasesCaseSensitive = false;
  };
  persistence = {
    libraryPath = "/media/porn-vault/lib/library";
    tempFolder = "tmp";
  };
  plugins = {
    events = {
      "scene:created" = [ ];
    };
    register = { };
  };
  processing = {
    bookmarkNewScenes = false;
    generatePreviewStrip = true;
  };
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/web-apps/porn-vault/default.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/web-apps/porn-vault/default.nix)


The portmaster package to use.

## `services.portmaster.profilePrefix` {#opt-services.portmaster.profilePrefix}

Prefix added to the display name of every declarative profile.

*Type:* string

*Default:* `""`

*Example:* `"[NixOS] "`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles}

Declarative per-application profiles keyed by logical name.

Profiles are imported through Portmaster's profile import API with
`allowReplace`. Package-derived regular expressions remain stable across
package updates. At least one entry in `packages` or `fingerprints` is
required. Changing a profile's normalized
fingerprints creates a different Portmaster identity and can leave the
previous imported profile behind. Removing a declaration does not delete
a previously imported profile.

The profiles are imported through the API address set with
`core/listenAddress` in `settings`; an address set only in
`settingsFile`, in `secretsFile` or with
`--api-address` in `extraArgs` is not used for this.

*Type:* attribute set of (submodule)

*Default:* `{ }`

*Example:*

``` nix
{
  Firefox = {
    packages = [
      {
        package = pkgs.firefox;
        directory = "lib/firefox";
      }
    ];
    settings.filter.defaultAction = "permit";
  };
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.fingerprints` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.fingerprints}

Additional Portmaster fingerprints for this profile. These are
merged with fingerprints generated from `packages`.

Portmaster fingerprints are ORed, not ANDed, so broad
fingerprints can match unrelated applications.

*Type:* list of (submodule)

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  {
    key = "CHROME_DESKTOP";
    operation = "equals";
    type = "env";
    value = "vesktop.desktop";
  }
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.fingerprints.*.key` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.fingerprints._.key}

Environment variable or metadata tag key. Required for `env` and
`tag` fingerprints, and invalid for `path` and `cmdline` fingerprints.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.fingerprints.*.operation` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.fingerprints._.operation}

Operation used to compare the fingerprint value.

*Type:* one of "equals", "prefix", "regex"

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.fingerprints.*.type` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.fingerprints._.type}

Portmaster fingerprint type.

*Type:* one of "path", "cmdline", "env", "tag"

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.fingerprints.*.value` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.fingerprints._.value}

The value to match against.

*Type:* string

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.name` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.name}

Human-readable Portmaster profile name.

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"‹name›"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.packages` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.packages}

Packages from which to derive Portmaster fingerprints.

A package can be specified directly for the default matching
behavior, or as an attribute set to customize its generated
fingerprint. Package-derived regular expressions do not include
a specific store hash or package version and also match
Nix-generated `.program-wrapped` executables by default.

*Type:* list of ((submodule) or package convertible to it)

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  pkgs.curl
  {
    package = pkgs.go;
    directory = "share/go/bin";
  }
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.packages.*.directory` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.packages._.directory}

Relative directory below the package output that contains the
executable. An empty string selects the output root.

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"bin"`

*Example:* `"share/go/bin"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.packages.*.name` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.packages._.name}

Executable name. Set this to `null` and disable `strictLast` to
match every path below `directory`.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `package.meta.mainProgram or package.pname`

*Example:* `"nmap"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.packages.*.package` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.packages._.package}

Package from which to derive a Portmaster fingerprint.

*Type:* package

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.packages.*.storeNameRegex` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.packages._.storeNameRegex}

Regular expression matching the package output name after the Nix
store hash. `null` matches the package's `pname` with an optional
version suffix.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Example:* `"python3[0-9.]*-umu-launcher-unwrapped-[0-9.]+"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.packages.*.strictHead` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.packages._.strictHead}

Anchor the generated regular expression at the beginning.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.packages.*.strictLast` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.packages._.strictLast}

Anchor the generated regular expression at the end.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.packages.*.type` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.packages._.type}

Fingerprint type used for the generated package regular expression.

*Type:* one of "path", "cmdline"

*Default:* `"path"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.packages.*.wrapped` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.packages._.wrapped}

Also match Nix wrapper names such as `.program-wrapped`.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.profiles.<name>.settings` {#opt-services.portmaster.profiles._name_.settings}

Per-application Portmaster settings for this profile, using the
upstream nested per-app configuration shape such as
`history.enable`, `filter.defaultAction`, or `spn.use`.
Global-only settings are rejected by Portmaster during sync.

Do not put secrets here; generated profile payloads are stored in
the Nix store.

*Type:* open submodule of (JSON value)

*Default:* `{ }`

*Example:*

``` nix
{
  filter = {
    defaultAction = "permit";
  };
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.secretsFile` {#opt-services.portmaster.secretsFile}

Sensitive global settings JSON file merged last into runtime
`config.json`, keeping secret values out of the Nix store.

*Type:* null or absolute path not in the Nix store

*Default:* `null`

*Example:* `"/run/secrets/portmaster-secrets.json"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.settings` {#opt-services.portmaster.settings}

Global Portmaster settings for runtime `config.json`.
Per-application profiles are managed by `profiles`.

Inputs are merged per Portmaster setting key and later inputs win:
this option, `settingsFile`, then `secretsFile`.
Nested objects are flattened first, so `core.devMode` and
`"core/devMode"` refer to the same setting.

When declarative configuration is active, the module owns runtime
`config.json`; global changes made only through the UI are not
preserved across service starts.

Do not put secrets here; values are stored in the Nix store. Use
`secretsFile` instead.

Upstream currently documents the available keys in
[basic\_config.go](https://github.com/safing/portmaster/blob/v2.2.1/base/config/basic_config.go#L10-L96).

*Type:* open submodule of (JSON value)

*Default:* `{ }`

*Example:*

``` nix
{
  "core/log/level" = "warning";
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.settings.devmode` {#opt-services.portmaster.settings.devmode}

Enable development mode for debugging. It turns off authentication
of the local API on 127.0.0.1:817, so every local process and user
gets full control over Portmaster, and pages served from
`localhost` can access the API. The packaged desktop client does
not require this option.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.settingsFile` {#opt-services.portmaster.settingsFile}

Additional global settings JSON file merged after `settings`.
Overlapping keys override values from that option.

*Type:* null or absolute path not in the Nix store

*Default:* `null`

*Example:* `"/run/secrets/portmaster-settings.json"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portmaster.stateDir` {#opt-services.portmaster.stateDir}

Directory used for Portmaster's mutable state, configuration, and logs.

*Type:* absolute path not in the Nix store

*Default:* `"/var/lib/portmaster"`

*Example:* `"/persist/portmaster"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/portmaster.nix)

## `services.portunus.dex.enable` {#opt-services.portunus.dex.enable}

Whether to enable Dex ldap connector.

To activate dex, first a search user must be created in the Portunus web ui
and then the password must to be set as the `DEX_SEARCH_USER_PASSWORD` environment variable
in the [services (D)](../../options/services-d/index.md#opt-services.dex.environmentFile) setting
.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

*Example:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/misc/portunus.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/misc/portunus.nix)

## `services.portunus.dex.oidcClients` {#opt-services.portunus.dex.oidcClients}

List of OIDC clients.

The OIDC secret must be set as the `DEX_CLIENT_${id}` environment variable
in the [services (D)](../../options/services-d/index.md#opt-services.dex.environmentFile) setting.

::: note
Make sure the id only contains characters that are allowed in an environment variable name, e.g. no -.
:::

*Type:* list of (submodule)

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  {
    id = "service";
    redirectURIs = [
      "https://example.com/client/oidc/callback"
    ];
  }
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/misc/portunus.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/misc/portunus.nix)

## `services.portunus.dex.oidcClients.*.callbackURL` {#opt-services.portunus.dex.oidcClients._.callbackURL}

URL where the OIDC client should redirect (deprecated, use redirectURIs)

ID of the OIDC client

*Type:* string

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/misc/portunus.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/misc/portunus.nix)

## `services.portunus.dex.oidcClients.*.redirectURIs` {#opt-services.portunus.dex.oidcClients._.redirectURIs}

URLs where the OIDC client should redirect

Port where dex should listen on.

## `services.portunus.ldap.searchUserName` {#opt-services.portunus.ldap.searchUserName}

The login name of the search user.
This user account must be configured in Portunus either manually or via seeding.

The DN of the topmost entry in your LDAP directory.

*Example:* `"dc=example,dc=org"`

## `services.portunus.ldap.tls` {#opt-services.portunus.ldap.tls}

Whether to enable LDAPS protocol.
This also adds two entries to the `/etc/hosts` file to point [services (P)](#opt-services.portunus.domain) to localhost,
so that CLIs and programs can use ldaps protocol and verify the certificate without opening the firewall port for the protocol.

This requires a TLS certificate for [services (P)](#opt-services.portunus.domain) to be configured via [security](../../options/security/index.md#opt-security.acme.certs).

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

Path where Portunus stores its state.

User account under which Portunus runs its webserver.

Whether to enable Porxie, an ATProto blob proxy for secure content delivery.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

*Example:* `true`

## `services.porxie.environmentFiles` {#opt-services.porxie.environmentFiles}

Files to load environment variables from. Use for secrets such as
`PORXIE_SERVER_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `PORXIE_POLICY_REQUEST_HEADERS`.

*Type:* list of absolute path

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.package` {#opt-services.porxie.package}

The porxie package to use.

*Type:* package

*Default:* `pkgs.porxie`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings` {#opt-services.porxie.settings}

Configuration for Porxie as environment variables. See the
[README](https://codeberg.org/Blooym/porxie/src/branch/main/README.md)
for detailed information about application configuration.

Secrets such as `settings.PORXIE_SERVER_ADMIN_PASSWORD` should be set via
`environmentFiles` rather than here, as values set here will
be readable in the Nix store.

*Type:* open submodule of attribute set of (null or string or boolean or signed integer)

*Default:* `{ }`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_ALLOWED_MIMETYPES` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_ALLOWED_MIMETYPES}

Blob mimetypes that can be served. Wildcards are supported "*/*", "image/\*", etc.

Validation is done loosely via content sniffing. Further validation can be done by a layer
above this proxy, such as an image transformation service. When inference fails, the blob's
type falls back to `application/octet-stream`. When that type is allowed, blobs failing
inference can still be served.

*Type:* null or (list of string)

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_CACHE_HEADER` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_CACHE_HEADER}

The Cache-Control header value to send alongside blob responses.

This does not affect internal cache lifetimes, only how downstream clients such as CDNs
and browsers are instructed to cache responses.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_HTTP_TIMEOUT` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_HTTP_TIMEOUT}

Maximum duration before blob fetch requests are timed out.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_MAX_SIZE` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_MAX_SIZE}

Maximum blob size that can be served.

This value cannot be set higher than the system's total memory.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_PROCESSING_TIMEOUT` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_BLOB_PROCESSING_TIMEOUT}

Maximum duration a blob can be processed by this server before aborting.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_ALLOCATION` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_ALLOCATION}

Total memory allocation for the internal cache.

Blobs are cached using an LFU policy. The most frequently requested blobs are kept longest when the cache reaches maximum size.

For production deployments, a CDN or caching layer in front of this server is
recommended for lower latency and better global availability.

The minimum value is 8mb and the maximum is the system's total memory.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_BLOB_TTI` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_BLOB_TTI}

How long blobs can be idle in the cache before expiring.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_IDENTITY_TTL` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_IDENTITY_TTL}

How long identity lookups (DID resolution, etc.) can be cached before expiring.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_OWNERSHIP_TTL` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_OWNERSHIP_TTL}

How long blob ownership can be cached before expiring.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_POLICY_TTL` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_CACHE_POLICY_TTL}

How long policy decisions can be cached before expiring.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_IDENTITY_PLC_URL` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_IDENTITY_PLC_URL}

URL of the PLC instance used for `did:plc` lookups.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_POLICY_FAIL_OPEN` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_POLICY_FAIL_OPEN}

Allow requests to proceed even if the policy service is unavailable.

Warning: enabling this means restricted blobs may be served when the policy service
is unavailable.

*Type:* null or boolean

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_POLICY_REQUEST_HEADERS` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_POLICY_REQUEST_HEADERS}

Headers sent alongside requests to the policy service.

Each header must be in the format `Name: value`.

As pipes are used as a delimiter, they cannot be contained in headers.

Should be set via `environmentFiles` for sensitive values such as API keys.

*Type:* null or (list of string)

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_POLICY_URL` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_POLICY_URL}

Policy service URL that DID+CID pairs will be checked against.

Requests are sent via XRPC to `<url>/xrpc/dev.blooym.porxie.getBlobPolicy`.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_SERVER_ADDRESS` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_SERVER_ADDRESS}

Address to bind the server to.

Use the `ip:` prefix for an IP address (e.g. `ip:127.0.0.1:6314`), or on UNIX
systems, the `unix:` prefix for a UNIX socket path (e.g. `unix:/run/porxie/porxie.sock`).

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"ip:127.0.0.1:6314"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

## `services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_SERVER_ADMIN_PASSWORD` {#opt-services.porxie.settings.PORXIE_SERVER_ADMIN_PASSWORD}

Admin password for authenticating privileged requests.

Authenticated requests always expect the username `admin` as per specification.

When not set, authenticated endpoints will be unavailable.

Should be set via `environmentFiles` rather than directly.

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/networking/porxie.nix)

*Default:* `"info"`

*Example:* `"warn"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix-tlspol.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix-tlspol.nix)

## `services.postfix-tlspol.settings.server.prefetch` {#opt-services.postfix-tlspol.settings.server.prefetch}

Whether to prefetch DNS records when the TTL of a cached record is about to expire.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `true`

*Example:* `false`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix-tlspol.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix-tlspol.nix)

## `services.postfix-tlspol.settings.server.socket-permissions` {#opt-services.postfix-tlspol.settings.server.socket-permissions}

Permissions to the UNIX socket, if configured.

::: note
Due to hardening on the systemd unit the socket can never be created world readable/writable.
:::

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"0660"`

*Read only*

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix-tlspol.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix-tlspol.nix)

## `services.postfix.aliasFiles` {#opt-services.postfix.aliasFiles}

Aliases' tables to be compiled and placed into /var/lib/postfix/conf.

*Type:* attribute set of absolute path

*Default:* `{ }`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.aliasMapType` {#opt-services.postfix.aliasMapType}

The format the alias map should have. Use regexp if you want to use regular expressions.

*Type:* one of "hash", "regexp", "pcre"

*Default:* `"hash"`

*Example:* `"regexp"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.canonical` {#opt-services.postfix.canonical}

Entries for the `canonical(5)` table.

*Type:* strings concatenated with "\\n"

*Default:* `""`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.dnsBlacklistOverrides` {#opt-services.postfix.dnsBlacklistOverrides}

contents of check\_client\_access for overriding dnsBlacklists

*Type:* strings concatenated with "\\n"

*Default:* `""`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.dnsBlacklists` {#opt-services.postfix.dnsBlacklists}

dns blacklist servers to use with smtpd\_client\_restrictions

*Type:* list of string

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.enable` {#opt-services.postfix.enable}

Whether to run the Postfix mail server.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.enableHeaderChecks` {#opt-services.postfix.enableHeaderChecks}

Whether to enable postfix header checks

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

*Example:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.enableSmtp` {#opt-services.postfix.enableSmtp}

Whether to enable the `smtp` service configured in the master.cf.

This service listens for plain text SMTP connections on port 25
and supports explicit TLS via StartTLS.

It is the primary port used by SMTP servers to exchange mail.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.enableSubmission` {#opt-services.postfix.enableSubmission}

Whether to enable the `submission` service configured in master.cf.

          This service listens for plain text SMTP connections on port 587
          and supports explicit TLS via StartTLS.

          It is a way for clients to login and submit mails after an inband
          connection upgrade using StartTLS.

          ::: {.warning}
          [RFC 8314](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8314) discourages the use
          of explicit TLS for mail submissionn.
          :::

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.enableSubmissions` {#opt-services.postfix.enableSubmissions}

Whether to enable the `submissions` service configured in master.cf.

This service listen for implicit TLS connections on port 465.

::: info
Per [RFC 8314](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8314) implicit TLS
is recommended for mail submission.
:::

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.extraAliases` {#opt-services.postfix.extraAliases}

Additional entries to put verbatim into aliases file, cf. man-page `aliases(8)`.

*Type:* strings concatenated with "\\n"

*Default:* `""`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.extraHeaderChecks` {#opt-services.postfix.extraHeaderChecks}

Extra lines to /etc/postfix/header\_checks file.

*Type:* strings concatenated with "\\n"

*Default:* `""`

*Example:* `"/^X-Spam-Flag:/ REDIRECT spam@example.com"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.extraMasterConf` {#opt-services.postfix.extraMasterConf}

Extra lines to append to the generated master.cf file.

*Type:* strings concatenated with "\\n"

*Default:* `""`

*Example:* `"submission inet n - n - - smtpd"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.group` {#opt-services.postfix.group}

What to call the Postfix group (must be used only for postfix).

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"postfix"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.headerChecks` {#opt-services.postfix.headerChecks}

Postfix header checks.

*Type:* list of (submodule)

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  {
    action = "REDIRECT spam@example.com";
    pattern = "/^X-Spam-Flag:/";
  }
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.headerChecks.*.action` {#opt-services.postfix.headerChecks._.action}

The action to be executed when the pattern is matched

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"DUNNO"`

*Example:* `"BCC mail@example.com"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.headerChecks.*.pattern` {#opt-services.postfix.headerChecks._.pattern}

A regexp pattern matching the header

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"/^.*/"`

*Example:* `"/^X-Mailer:/"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.localRecipients` {#opt-services.postfix.localRecipients}

List of accepted local users. Specify a bare username, an
`"@domain.tld"` wild-card, or a complete
`"user@domain.tld"` address. If set, these names end
up in the local recipient map -- see the `local(8)` man-page -- and
effectively replace the system user database lookup that's otherwise
used by default.

*Type:* null or (list of string)

*Default:* `null`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.mapFiles` {#opt-services.postfix.mapFiles}

Maps to be compiled and placed into /var/lib/postfix/conf.

*Type:* attribute set of absolute path

*Default:* `{ }`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.package` {#opt-services.postfix.package}

The postfix package to use.

*Type:* package

*Default:* `pkgs.postfix`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.postmasterAlias` {#opt-services.postfix.postmasterAlias}

Who should receive postmaster e-mail. Multiple values can be added by
separating values with comma.

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"root"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.rootAlias` {#opt-services.postfix.rootAlias}

Who should receive root e-mail. Blank for no redirection.
Multiple values can be added by separating values with comma.

*Type:* string

*Default:* `""`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.setSendmail` {#opt-services.postfix.setSendmail}

Whether to set the system sendmail to postfix's.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.setgidGroup` {#opt-services.postfix.setgidGroup}

How to call postfix setgid group (for postdrop). Should
be uniquely used group.

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"postdrop"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main}

The main.cf configuration file as key value set.

Null values will not be rendered.

::: tip
Check `postconf -d` for the default values of all settings.
:::

*Type:* open submodule of attribute set of (null or boolean or signed integer or absolute path or string or list of string)

*Example:*

``` nix
{
  mail_owner = "postfix";
  smtp_tls_security_level = "may";
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.message_size_limit` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.message_size_limit}

Maximum size of an email message in bytes.

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#message\_size\_limit](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#message_size_limit)

*Type:* null or signed integer

*Default:* `10240000`

*Example:* `52428800`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.mydestination` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.mydestination}

List of domain names intended for local delivery using /etc/passwd and /etc/aliases.

::: warning
Do not include [virtual](https://www.postfix.org/VIRTUAL_README.html) domains in this list.
:::

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#mydestination](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#mydestination)

*Type:* null or string or list of string

*Default:*

``` nix
[
  "$myhostname"
  "localhost.$mydomain"
  "localhost"
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.myhostname` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.myhostname}

The internet hostname of this mail system.

Leave unset to default to the system hostname with the `mydomain` suffix.

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#myhostname](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#myhostname)

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `null`

*Example:* `"mail.example.com"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.mynetworks` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.mynetworks}

List of trusted remote SMTP clients, that are allowed to relay mail.

Leave unset to let Postfix populate this list based on the `mynetworks_style` setting.

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#mynetworks](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#mynetworks)

*Type:* null or (list of string)

*Default:* `null`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  "127.0.0.0/8"
  "::1"
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.mynetworks_style` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.mynetworks_style}

The method used for generating the default value for `mynetworks`, if that option is unset.

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#mynetworks\_style](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#mynetworks_style)

*Type:* null or one of "host", "subnet", "class"

*Default:* `"host"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.recipient_delimiter` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.recipient_delimiter}

Set of characters used as the delimiters for address extensions.

This allows creating different forwarding rules per extension.

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#recipient\_delimiter](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#recipient_delimiter)

*Type:* null or string

*Default:* `""`

*Example:* `"+"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.relay_domains` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.relay_domains}

List of domains delivered via the relay transport.

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#relay\_domains](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#relay_domains)

*Type:* null or (list of string)

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  "lists.example.com"
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.relayhost` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.relayhost}

List of hosts to use for relaying outbound mail.

::: note
Putting the hostname in angled brackets, e.g. `[relay.example.com]`, turns off MX and SRV lookups for the hostname.
:::

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#relayhost](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#relayhost)

*Type:* null or (list of string)

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  "[relay.example.com]:587"
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.smtp_tls_CAfile` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.smtp_tls_CAfile}

File containing CA certificates of root CAs trusted to sign either remote SMTP server certificates or intermediate CA certificates.

Defaults to the system CA bundle that is managed through the `security.pki` options.

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtp\_tls\_CAfile](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtp_tls_CAfile)

*Type:* absolute path

*Default:*

``` nix
config.security.pki.caBundle
```

*Example:*

``` nix
${pkgs.cacert}/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.smtp_tls_security_level` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.smtp_tls_security_level}

The client TLS security level.

::: tip
Use `dane` with a local DNSSEC validating DNS resolver enabled.
:::

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtp\_tls\_security\_level](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtp_tls_security_level)

*Type:* one of "none", "may", "encrypt", "dane", "dane-only", "fingerprint", "verify", "secure"

*Default:* `"may"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.smtpd_tls_chain_files` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.smtpd_tls_chain_files}

List of paths to the server private keys and certificates.

::: caution
The order of items matters and a private key must always be followed by the corresponding certificate.
:::

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtpd\_tls\_chain\_files](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtpd_tls_chain_files)

*Type:* list of absolute path

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  "/var/lib/acme/mail.example.com/privkey.pem"
  "/var/lib/acme/mail.example.com/fullchain.pem"
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.main.smtpd_tls_security_level` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.main.smtpd_tls_security_level}

The server TLS security level. Enable TLS by configuring at least `may`.

[https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtpd\_tls\_security\_level](https://www.postfix.org/postconf.5.html#smtpd_tls_security_level)

*Type:* one of "none", "may", "encrypt"

*Default:*

``` nix
if config.services.postfix.settings.main.smtpd_tls_chain_files != [ ] then "may" else "none"
```

*Example:* `"may"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.master` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.master}

The `master.cf` configuration file as an attribute set of service
defitions

::: tip
Check [https://www.postfix.org/master.5.html](https://www.postfix.org/master.5.html) for possible settings.
:::

*Type:* attribute set of (submodule)

*Default:* `{ }`

*Example:*

``` nix
{
  submission = {
    args = [
      "-o"
      "smtpd_tls_security_level=encrypt"
    ];
    type = "inet";
  };
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.args` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.master._name_.args}

Arguments to pass to the `command`. There is no shell
processing involved and shell syntax is passed verbatim to the
process.

*Type:* list of string

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  "-o"
  "smtp_helo_timeout=5"
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.chroot` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.master._name_.chroot}

Whether the service is chrooted to have only access to the
`services.postfix.queueDir` and the closure of
store paths specified by the `program` option.

*Type:* boolean

*Example:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.command` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.master._name_.command}

A program name specifying a Postfix service/daemon process.
By default it's the attribute `name`.

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"‹name›"`

*Example:* `"smtpd"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.maxproc` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.master._name_.maxproc}

The maximum number of processes to spawn for this service. If the
value is `0` it doesn't have any limit. If
`null` is given it uses the postfix default of
`100`.

*Type:* signed integer

*Example:* `1`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.name` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.master._name_.name}

The name of the service to run. Defaults to the attribute set key.

*Type:* string

*Default:* `"‹name›"`

*Example:* `"smtp"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.private` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.master._name_.private}

Whether the service's sockets and storage directory is restricted to
be only available via the mail system. If `null` is
given it uses the postfix default `true`.

*Type:* boolean

*Example:* `false`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.privileged` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.master._name_.privileged}

*Type:* boolean

*Example:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.type` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.master._name_.type}

The type of the service

*Type:* one of "inet", "unix", "unix-dgram", "fifo", "pass"

*Default:* `"unix"`

*Example:* `"inet"`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.wakeup` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.master._name_.wakeup}

Automatically wake up the service after the specified number of
seconds. If `0` is given, never wake the service
up.

*Type:* signed integer

*Example:* `60`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.settings.master.<name>.wakeupUnusedComponent` {#opt-services.postfix.settings.master._name_.wakeupUnusedComponent}

If set to `false` the component will only be woken
up if it is used. This is equivalent to postfix' notion of adding a
question mark behind the wakeup time in
`master.cf`

*Type:* boolean

*Example:* `false`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/mail/postfix.nix)

## `services.postfix.submissionOptions` {#opt-services.postfix.submissionOptions}

::: note
The `environment.PGWS_JWT_SECRET` option is blocked.

The password to authenticate to PostgreSQL with.

The file must be a valid `.pgpass` file as described in:
[https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-pgpass.html](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-pgpass.html)

In most cases, the following will be enough:

```
*:*:*:*:<password>
```

*Type:* null or absolute path not in the Nix store

## `services.postgresql.authentication` {#opt-services.postgresql.authentication}

Defines how users authenticate themselves to the server. See the
[PostgreSQL documentation for pg\_hba.conf](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/auth-pg-hba-conf.html)
for details on the expected format of this option. By default,
peer based authentication will be used for users connecting
via the Unix socket, and md5 password authentication will be
used for users connecting via TCP. Any added rules will be
inserted above the default rules. If you'd like to replace the
default rules entirely, you can use `lib.mkForce` in your
module.

*Type:* strings concatenated with "\\n"

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix)

## `services.postgresql.ensureDatabases` {#opt-services.postgresql.ensureDatabases}

Ensures that the specified databases exist.
This option will never delete existing databases, especially not when the value of this
option is changed. This means that databases created once through this option or
otherwise have to be removed manually.

*Type:* list of string

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  "gitea"
  "nextcloud"
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix)

## `services.postgresql.ensureUsers` {#opt-services.postgresql.ensureUsers}

Ensures that the specified users exist.
The PostgreSQL users will be identified using peer authentication. This authenticates the Unix user with the
same name only, and that without the need for a password.
This option will never delete existing users or remove DB ownership of databases
once granted with `ensureDBOwnership = true;`. This means that this must be
cleaned up manually when changing after changing the config in here.

*Type:* list of (submodule)

*Default:* `[ ]`

*Example:*

``` nix
[
  {
    name = "nextcloud";
  }
  {
    name = "superuser";
    ensureDBOwnership = true;
  }
]
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix)

## `services.postgresql.ensureUsers.*.ensureClauses` {#opt-services.postgresql.ensureUsers._.ensureClauses}

An attrset of clauses to grant to the user. Under the hood this uses the
[ALTER USER syntax](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-alteruser.html) for each attrName where
the attrValue is true in the attrSet:
`ALTER USER user.name WITH attrName`

*Type:* open submodule of attribute set of (string or signed integer or boolean)

*Default:* `{ }`

*Example:*

``` nix
{
  superuser = true;
  createrole = true;
  createdb = true;
  connection_limit = 5;

  # SCRAM-SHA-256 hashed password for "password"
  # Generate hashes using PostgreSQL or a dedicated script rather than storing passwords in plain text.
  password = "SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:SZEJF5Si4QZ6l4fedrZZWQ==$6u3PWVcz+dts+NdpByPIjKa4CaSnoXGG3M2vpo76bVU=:WSZ0iGUCmVtKYVvNX0pFOp/60IgsdJ+90Y67Eun+QE0=";
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix)

## `services.postgresql.ensureUsers.*.ensureDBOwnership` {#opt-services.postgresql.ensureUsers._.ensureDBOwnership}

## `services.postgresql.identMap` {#opt-services.postgresql.identMap}

Defines the mapping from system users to database users.

See the [auth doc](https://postgresql.org/docs/current/auth-username-maps.html).

There is a default map "postgres" which is used for local peer authentication

For example, to allow the root user to login as the postgres superuser, add:

The package being used by postgresql.

``` nix
else if versionAtLeast config.system.stateVersion "25.11" then
```

## `services.postgresql.settings` {#opt-services.postgresql.settings}

PostgreSQL configuration. Refer to
[https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/config-setting.html#CONFIG-SETTING-CONFIGURATION-FILE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/config-setting.html#CONFIG-SETTING-CONFIGURATION-FILE)
for an overview of `postgresql.conf`.

::: note
String values will automatically be enclosed in single quotes. Single quotes will be
escaped with two single quotes as described by the upstream documentation linked above.
:::

*Type:* open submodule of attribute set of (boolean or floating point number or signed integer or string)

``` nix
{
  log_connections = true;
  log_statement = "all";
  logging_collector = true;
  log_disconnections = true;
  log_destination = lib.mkForce "syslog";
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix)

## `services.postgresql.settings.log_line_prefix` {#opt-services.postgresql.settings.log_line_prefix}

A printf-style string that is output at the beginning of each log line.

not include the timestamp, because journal has it anyway.

*Type:* string

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix)

The port on which PostgreSQL listens.

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix)

## `services.postgresql.settings.shared_preload_libraries` {#opt-services.postgresql.settings.shared_preload_libraries}

List of libraries to be preloaded.

*Type:* null or (strings concatenated with "," or (list of string) convertible to it)

*Default:* `null`

*Example:* `[ "auto_explain" "anon" ]`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix)

## `services.postgresql.systemCallFilter` {#opt-services.postgresql.systemCallFilter}

Configures the syscall filter for `postgresql.service`. The keys are
declarations for `SystemCallFilter` as described in `systemd.exec(5)`.

The value is a boolean: `true` adds the attribute name to the syscall filter-set,
`false` doesn't. This is done to allow downstream configurations to turn off
restrictions made here. E.g. with

``` nix
{
  services.postgresql.systemCallFilter."~@resources" = false;
}
```

it's possible to remove the restriction on `@resources` (keep in mind that
`@system-service` implies `@resources`).

As described in the section for [services (P)](#opt-services.postgresql.systemCallFilter._name_.priority),
the ordering matters. Hence, it's also possible to specify customizations with

``` nix
{
  services.postgresql.systemCallFilter = {
    "foobar" = { enable = true; priority = 23; };
  };
}
```

[services (P)](#opt-services.postgresql.systemCallFilter._name_.enable) is the flag whether
or not it will be added to the `SystemCallFilter` of `postgresql.service`.

Settings with a higher priority are added after filter settings with a lower
priority. Hence, syscall groups with a higher priority can discard declarations
with a lower priority.

By default, syscall groups (i.e. attribute names starting with `@`) are added
*before* negated groups (i.e. `~@` as prefix) *before* syscall names
and negations.

*Type:* attribute set of ((submodule) or boolean convertible to it)

*Default:*

``` nix
{
  "@system-service" = true;
  "~@privileged" = true;
  "~@resources" = true;
}
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix)

## `services.postgresql.systemCallFilter.<name>.enable` {#opt-services.postgresql.systemCallFilter._name_.enable}

Whether to enable ‹name› in postgresql's syscall filter.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `false`

*Example:* `true`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix)

## `services.postgresql.systemCallFilter.<name>.priority` {#opt-services.postgresql.systemCallFilter._name_.priority}

Set the priority of the system call filter setting. Later declarations
override earlier ones, e.g.

``` ini
[Service]
SystemCallFilter=~read write
SystemCallFilter=write
```

results in a service where *only* `read` is not allowed.

The ordering in the unit file is controlled by this option: the higher
the number, the later it will be added to the filterset.

By default, depending on the prefix a priority is assigned: usually, call-groups
(starting with `@`) are used to allow/deny a larger set of syscalls and later
on single syscalls are configured for exceptions. Hence, syscall groups
and negative groups are placed before individual syscalls by default.

*Type:* signed integer

*Default:*

``` nix
if hasPrefix "@" name then 500 else if hasPrefix "~@" name then 1000 else 1500
```

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/databases/postgresql.nix)

## `services.postgresqlBackup.backupAll` {#opt-services.postgresqlBackup.backupAll}

Backup all databases using pg\_dumpall.
This option is mutual exclusive to
`services.postgresqlBackup.databases`.
The resulting backup dump will have the name all.sql.gz.
This option is the default if no databases are specified.

*Type:* boolean

*Default:* `services.postgresqlBackup.databases == []`

*Declared by:* [`nixos/modules/services/backup/postgresql-backup.nix`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/services/backup/postgresql-backup.nix)

## `services.postgresqlBackup.compression` {#opt-services.postgresqlBackup.compression}

The type of compression to use on the generated database dump.
